name: Cross-venue lead-lag: follower quoting and price-discovery signals
one_line: Beyond matched-pair arb: LP structures over equivalence and subset relations, and single-venue quoting off the deeper venue's price where locked arb is impractical.
scope: Cover the NON-locked use of other venues: which venue leads price discovery by category (Kalshi, Polymarket US BBO feed, Betfair, sportsbooks, Pinnacle), follower quoting / stale-quote picking on the lagging venue, using the free Polymarket US BBO or Kalshi book as a fair-value input for international Polymarket quotes, measured lead-lag magnitudes and half-lives, and why this needs no capital on the second venue. Boundary: locked two-leg structures are cross-venue-locked-arbitrage; sportsbook-anchored quoting of sports is sportsbook-anchored-sports-mm (cross-reference, do not repeat).

parent_scope: Cover (1) locked structures: semantic matching across venues, equivalence vs strict-subset vs negative-risk constructions, LP payoff-floor solver, realised evidence (796 structures in nine days, 0.52% capital-weighted; 2-4% persistent deviations), annualising against the ~4-7% settlement discount, settlement-rule mismatches as the whole risk (2024 election, DNP props, void conventions); (2) lead-lag: Kalshi depth 3-5x on US sports with 2-3 s Polymarket lag, Polymarket leading in 2024 election, large-trade imbalance signals, Wintermute closing gaps; (3) the international-vs-US Polymarket books as unconnected venues and the no-auth US BBO feed as a free signal. Boundary: options venues are options-implied-relative-value; sportsbook lines as fair value for quoting are sportsbook-anchored-sports-mm; promo hedging is fee-tier-taker-incentives.
critic_notes: SPLIT cross-venue-arbitrage-leadlag into (a) locked cross-venue structures (widely practised and crowded: 301 GitHub repos for 'polymarket kalshi arbitrage', paid scanners; no documented realised PnL) and (b) lead-lag follower quoting and signals. Demote the international-vs-US order-book sub-variant to a flagged note or the speculative band: E5 and E9 agree it needs two properly domiciled entities and a US person cannot lawfully touch the international venue. Add a missing sub-variant: cross-venue short-dated crypto pairs, where Polymarket settles on a Chainlink TWAP and Kalshi on the average of 60 one-second CF Benchmarks RTI prints (E5 key fact 10), so the 'arb' carries index-basis risk.

cross-venue-arbitrage-leadlag: 'Emerging' understates locked Polymarket-Kalshi arbitrage as a practice (crowded, tooled, already in the owner's suite) and overstates the international-vs-US sub-variant (not lawfully runnable by one person). One label hides both; note also that E5 found no documented cross-venue arbitrageur PnL anywhere, so 'Established' would apply to activity, not to proven profit.

cross-venue-arbitrage-leadlag, sub-variant 'international vs US order-book gap and BBO signal': legally unavailable to a single person and evidenced by one indicative endpoint; keep the free US BBO feed as a signal note only.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Cross-venue linear-program arbitrage over the joint outcome space, including subset relations
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Go beyond matched-pair Polymarket/Kalshi arbitrage: build a semantic identity layer across venues and solve an LP for a guaranteed payoff floor over equivalence, subset and negative-risk structures.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Match events across Polymarket, Kalshi and long-tail venues into equivalence classes and strict-subset relations (different resolution rules make many 'same' markets subsets of each other). For each structure solve an LP over outcome space for the cheapest portfolio with payoff floor > cost, using executable book prices. Hold to resolution or unwind on convergence. Resolution-rule differences are modelled as explicit states rather than ignored.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Law-of-one-price violations persisting because capital is segmented by venue, KYC and collateral type, and because semantically similar contracts are not fungible.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Most bots do pairwise equivalent-market arb; subset and multi-leg LP structures are less crowded, and 1,200-1,500 new matched pairs now appear per 42-day window.

evidence.title: Semantic Non-Fungibility and Violations of the Law of One Price in Prediction Markets (Gebele, Matthes), arXiv
evidence.supports: 102,275 events on 10 venues (2018..Aug-2025): ~6% cross-listed; 1,501 equivalence classes, 1,645 subset sets, 1,123 negative-risk constructions; median execution-adjusted deviations 2-4% even in liquid pairs, often persisting nearly the whole overlap; many opportunities >200% APY; simulated mechanical strategy 1,218.66% cumulative over 15 trades / 800 days (tiny n); ~8% of Polymarket markets have an equivalent elsewhere vs 2% of Kalshi's.

evidence.title: Combinatorial Arbitrage Between Prediction Markets (Krasovec), Univ. of Ljubljana thesis
evidence.supports: Nine-day passive observation across Kalshi, Polymarket, Predict, Limitless: 796 arbitrage structures, modelled payoff floor $6,148, capital-weighted return 0.52%; of 308 resolved structures 306 paid at or above floor ($533 vs $522 floor); one shortfall ($0.38) was caused by settlement-rule differences.

evidence.title: Price Discovery and Trading in Modern Prediction Markets (Ng, Peng, Tao, Zhou), SSRN via Crossref abstract
evidence.supports: Significant price disparities across Polymarket, Kalshi, PredictIt, Robinhood before the 2024 election imply economically meaningful arbitrage.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Semantic risk is the whole risk (Polymarket resolved the 2024 election on network calls, Kalshi on inauguration); capital locked on two venues to resolution, so the 0.52% per-structure return must beat the ~4-7% annualised settlement discount; venue/legal access; fees on both sides.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Passive logger like the thesis: 2 weeks, record structures with floor > cost net of both venues' fees, track realised payoff vs floor and days-to-resolution to get an annualised, capital-weighted figure.
raw_discovery_candidates.flags: Requires accounts on multiple venues; geo/KYC restrictions apply per venue.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Cross-venue lead-lag quoting (Kalshi depth leads Polymarket)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Reprice Polymarket quotes off the deeper venue within its 2-3 second lag instead of chasing locked arbitrage.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: For US sports and some macro contracts Kalshi carries several times Polymarket's depth, and Polymarket reprices a couple of seconds later. Rather than buying both venues for a locked spread (capital on two venues, different resolution rules, fees on both), the agent uses Kalshi's book as fair value and makes or takes on Polymarket only. Institutional makers already move capital dynamically between the two. Practitioners report 5-8c gaps on identical outcomes at times.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Price discovery happens on the deeper book; Polymarket is the follower in sports.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Single-venue execution removes the settlement-mismatch and capital-lock problems that make pure cross-venue arb hard for small teams.

raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Record both books for 30 matched sports contracts; estimate Granger-style lead-lag and the PnL of a Polymarket-only follower after 0.05 fees.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Cross-venue lead-lag: trade the lagging venue on the leader's large-trade flow
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Polymarket leads Kalshi in price discovery when liquidity is high, and net order imbalance from large trades predicts returns - trade the follower directionally rather than waiting for a locked arb.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Stream signed large trades on both venues (on-chain OrderFilled for Polymarket ground truth), compute rolling net large-trade imbalance per matched contract, and enter the lagging venue in the leader's direction with a short holding period. The venue with the larger directional large-trade flow is treated as leader for that window. Exit on convergence or time stop.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Segmented participants and slower repricing on the follower; informed large traders concentrate where depth is.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It monetises cross-venue gaps that never become risk-free arbitrage (the common case), using public flow data.

evidence.title: Price Discovery and Trading in Modern Prediction Markets (Ng, Peng, Tao, Zhou), SSRN via Crossref abstract
evidence.supports: Polymarket leads Kalshi in price discovery, particularly when liquidity and activity are high; net order imbalance from large trades strongly predicts subsequent returns; the venue with greater directional large-trade flow leads.

evidence.title: The Anatomy of a Blockchain Prediction Market: Polymarket in the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election (Tsang, Yang), arXiv
evidence.supports: Price impact: ~$9.1M of corrected flow moved the October Trump contract 5 pts (naive estimate $15.6M); $1M moved price 4-15 pts in January vs ~0.5 pt in October; naive volume overstates turnover 2.45x (median 3.08x) - flow signals must use turnover, not OrderFilled sums.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Evidence is from one event (2024 election) and abstract-level; costs not reported; leadership may have shifted after Kalshi's 2025-26 growth; the French-whale episode shows the leader can also be the distorted venue (10-15 pts above competitors per Abid, SSRN 6670638).
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Hasbrouck information-share / Granger test on 50 currently matched contracts using 1-minute mids; then an event-study of follower returns after top-decile large-trade imbalance on the leader, net of follower spread.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: International vs US order-book gap: cross-book arbitrage and free lead-lag signal
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: The same NFL game trades on two unconnected Polymarket books with different fees, collateral and crowds; arbitrage it if you legally hold both accounts, otherwise use the no-auth US BBO feed as a fair-value signal for quoting the international book.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Polymarket.com (pUSD on Polygon, non-US users) and the Polymarket US app/exchange (USD, CFTC DCM/DCO, US residents) are separate products with unconnected accounts and separate central limit order books. On 2026-09-20 during Bengals-Texans, fetches seconds apart showed US 0.880 bid / 0.885 ask (open interest 1.13M contracts, 2.89M traded) against international 0.89 bid / 0.90 ask ($2.71M volume) - indicative only, non-simultaneous, side mapping not verified. Fee regimes differ sharply: the international NFL markets showed zero fees that day, the US book charges taker theta 0.0695 and pays makers theta 0.0125, and each book has its own liquidity-reward schedule. An operator with a US entity and a non-US affiliate can lock gaps or, more practically, quote as maker on both and let one book hedge the other. A team with access to only one side can still stream gateway.polymarket.us/v1/markets/{slug}/bbo (public) as an input to its international sports quoting.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Segmented participant pools (US retail app users vs global crypto-native traders) and legal barriers that stop most arbitrageurs from holding both accounts.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: US-book volume on NFL is already comparable to the international book, so the second price is informative; most international LPs do not consume it.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Legal access is the binding constraint; USD and pUSD funding loops are slow (wires/ACH vs bridge) so inventory drifts; both books have matching delays (sports 1 s internationally); contract specs and settlement rules can differ (US uses a Settlement Committee and Last Fair Market Price for voids, international uses UMA).
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Log both public BBO feeds with synchronized timestamps for one NFL week and measure gap frequency net of US taker fee, plus lead-lag cross-correlation at 1-10 s horizons.
raw_discovery_candidates.flags: Polymarket.com is not available to US residents and the US venue is built for US residents; one natural person cannot lawfully hold both. CoinDesk/Allium report $571M traded by US-linked wallets on the international site in 12 months via VPN - this is a ToS violation detected by IP blocking and on-chain behavioural analysis; do not build on it.
